findings.title: Keyed reads discard cancellation in the required unchanged dependency
findings.problem: The profile admits keyed reads and requires cancellation to reach the driver, while claiming no DALgo2SQL release is needed. At the pinned release and current authoritative main, database and transaction Get/GetMulti/Exists pass sql.DB.Query or Tx.Query; getSingle and executeExists discard context. Forwarding a browser signal through Worker/Cloud does not cancel those SQL calls or connection-pool waits. DTQL uses QueryContext, so its success would not prove the keyed route.
findings.smallest_fix: Explicitly add a bounded cancellation dependency task for all admitted keyed routes (context-aware QueryContext, including transaction and batch paths), or route these reads through an equivalent secured context-aware query path. Remove the unconditional no-upstream-change assertion. Retain a real driver cancellation acceptance test for both DTQL and keyed routes, including cancellation while waiting for a connection.
findings.falsifier: An inspected admitted implementation routes every permitted keyed operation through a context-aware executor, with actual cancellation evidence.

findings.title: Paging requires a generated key name that the client cannot discover
findings.problem: The client is required to issue deterministic order by the configured serving key, but its collision-allocated name may differ per table. The proposal puts the only map in generated server-local YAML, deliberately leaves provider models unchanged, and adds no checked client discovery mechanism. Current database metadata lists collections/capabilities/endpoints; the schema has no record-key designation. Seeing helper-looking field names cannot distinguish a native collision from the generated helper. Offset pages cannot safely guess the field or use native id as a substitute.
findings.smallest_fix: Prefer having the configured Cloud/library read profile supply and enforce deterministic serving-key order for ordinary W1 pages from the mounted map, defining refusal or tie-break behavior for caller ordering. Alternatively expose a small verified read-only key-map projection tied to the runtime snapshot and explicitly assign its consumer. Keep YAML authoritative and add a helper-collision pagination fixture proving no duplicates/skips across pages.
findings.falsifier: The architecture names an existing verified client-visible mapping, or server-owned order enforcement, and demonstrates collision-safe page requests without heuristics.

findings.title: Continuation pins omit the manifest that controls record identity and returned types
findings.problem: All three proposed pins can remain equal while runtime YAML changes: provider revision and native/serving SQLite hashes do not bind the generated record_keys map or schema types. The proposal itself adds manifestSha256 and verifies it at mount, but never puts it in the client snapshot identity. A deployment with the same SQLite bytes and a changed key mapping can return different API keys; changing a declared boolean field changes 0/1 to false/true through coerceToSchema. Both deployments pass the proposed guard, so a saved scenario or continuation can mix interpretations under apparently identical pins.
findings.smallest_fix: Bind the existing manifest hash into the guarded snapshot identity (a manifest pin or one aggregate runtime-artifact digest covering SQLite plus YAML; keep native-source and serving-file digest meanings clear). Persist and check that identity on every continuation and saved scenario. Add a negative fixture with unchanged provider/source/SQLite pins but changed manifest map/type that must return snapshot_mismatch before SQL.
findings.falsifier: A checked invariant proves manifest semantics cannot differ for identical accepted pins, or the request/response snapshot identity explicitly includes the mounted manifest.

findings.title: Configured query restrictions must also drive discovery and human query links
findings.problem: r2 adds W1-only refusal of relational/cross-database queries and requires pin headers for admitted reads, while preserving discovery and profile surfaces. Current advertisesJoins is driven by relationalRefusal, and discovery/database metadata emits its result as joins/aggregation. A separate W1 guard in the newly proposed handler path does not automatically change that predicate. Current human collections also emit a GET /query link whenever db.CanQuery is true; following that normal hyperlink cannot provide the mandatory pins and the route may itself be refused. The proposal does not yet assign the new profile to these existing advertised surfaces, leaving an internally contradictory discovery/UI contract.
findings.smallest_fix: Use one profile-aware admission predicate for both execution and advertisesJoins, so W1 joins and aggregation are false while ordinary DTQL query/read capability remains truthful. Preserve non-W1 capability values and global features available to other databases. Suppress QueryURL for bounded-immutable W1 collections (the template already conditionally omits it); do not place snapshot pins into URLs or invent a new browser query flow. Add these surfaces to the changed-file/acceptance matrix and test W1 plus a legacy database together, including initial query-unavailable and final published states.
findings.falsifier: The revised architecture explicitly binds discovery and human link generation to the same configured profile and requires coherent output fixtures.
